title: The Withdrawal Rate That Decides If Your Retirement Money Runs Out
description:
A $1 million retirement portfolio can last indefinitely at one withdrawal rate, or run dry in under twenty years at another - same market, same balance. We run the actual math across five withdrawal rates and show exactly where the cliff is.

This video uses AI-generated narration and visuals.

#Shorts #retirement #4percentrule #personalfinance

segments.text: A one million dollar retirement account. Same portfolio, same market. At one withdrawal rate it can last indefinitely. At another, it runs out in nineteen years.
The rate that decides this isn't the market's return. It's simply how much of the balance you take out each year.
As long as what you withdraw stays under what the portfolio earns, the balance can keep growing. The moment it doesn't, the countdown starts.
At three percent, it's still growing after sixty years. At four, it lasts forty-five. At seven, just nineteen.

slide.headline: Years until a $1M portfolio is empty

segments.text: Here's what four percent actually looks like, year by year, assuming a modest three percent real return after inflation.
It grinds down slowly at first, then falls off a cliff in the final decade, as the shrinking balance keeps earning less each year.
One number, chosen at the start, quietly decides whether your money outlives you, or the other way around.
